newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: African leaders pledge financial help for Kabila.
newsitem.headline: African leaders pledge financial help for Kabila.

text.p: A summit of eight African heads of state has pledged short-term financial support to help President Laurent Kabila rebuild the former Zaire, drained by decades of corruption and neglect.

The leaders of Uganda, Rwanda, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Namibia, Mozambique, Eritrea and Central African Republic met in Kinshasa on Sunday and voiced support for the new ruler of Africa's third largest nation, renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

"The heads of states and governments committed themselves to providing, within their means, concrete material and financial support to the Democratic Republic of the Congo," the summit said in its final communique.
"(They were) fully aware that while Congo does not require continued assistance, it needs timely support without attached strings and preconditions to overcome urgent challenges."
Kabila toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko after a seven-month military campaign in May.
Major donors shunned Mobutu's Zaire because of repeated human rights violations and lack of democracy. They have said aid could be restored if Kabila improves human rights.

Kabila's government has said it will not make repayments on the country's $14 billion foreign debt for now. It says a commission has been set up to audit the internal and the external debt before it can hold talks with donors in September.
The summit urged that Kabila be given time. "Ample time will be required to reverse 30 years of decline and destruction in order to build effective national institutions," it said.
Gabon and Ethiopia were also represented.
